verdict.rationale: Proton Pass ships an official CLI that lets scripts and headless environments retrieve secrets and items programmatically, so an agent can query the vault without screen-scraping the app. The evidence does not show a local endpoint or daemon an agent can query, and it does not show TOTP codes being retrievable through the CLI; TOTP generation is documented only as an app feature. Missing for 10: a documented local query endpoint or agent-facing interface, CLI retrieval of TOTP codes, and independent or hands-on corroboration of agent use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can expose the vault through a local programmatic endpoint an agent can query for codes and secrets without screen-scraping the app

citations.quote: the CLI enables you to securely retrieve secrets and other items across scripts, deployments, and continuous integration/ continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines.
With Proton Pass CLI, credentials can be injected directly into scripts, deployments, and CI/CD pipelines without exposing secrets in plaintext, shell, logs, or command history.
Work in CI/CD, servers, containers, and headless environments
View, create, update, and delete items including passwords, secure notes, credit cards, identities, WiFi entries, custom items, and stored SSH-key items
